findings.description: The reducer drops findings using a stable symbol anchor and a separate anchor_line, such as {"anchor":"src/foo.py:parse","anchor_line":42}. It forwards the symbol anchor, which citations() cannot parse, and never reads anchor_line.
findings.failure_mode: Correct adversarial findings contribute no citations, so review-catch reports caught defects as missed and understates recall.
findings.suggested_fix: Read anchor_line and anchor_line_end, extract the file component from the stable anchor, and emit a normalized file:line[-line] citation.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: all_pass ignores both the command exit code and timed_out whenever output contains a parseable summary. For example, a command that emits '1..1\nok 1 example\n' and then exits 1 is treated as fully passing.
findings.failure_mode: A runner failure after reporting test outcomes can produce an accurate APPROVED verdict or a green refactor suite. run_suite also exposes passing counts without the failing exit status in grade.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Require rc == 0 and timed_out == false for suite success, and propagate unsuccessful execution into the published result even when a summary was parsed.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The grader rewrites `python3 -m pytest` to `python3 -I -s -m pytest` (container) or `python3 -P -m pytest` (host). Both -I and -P remove the cwd entry that plain `python3 -m pytest` prepends to sys.path. Tests that import repo-root packages (e.g. `import tools.x` from a Loa checkout, without a conftest/pyproject that fixes sys.path) collect fine under the seeders' proof (`env -i … python3 -m pytest`, per seed-bugfix-tasks.sh/seed-refactor-tasks.sh headers) but fail with ImportError only inside the grader.
findings.failure_mode: A task proven red/green by seed-bugfix-tasks.sh grades every submission, including the reference patch, as 0/N with collection errors; self-check reference FAILs for an otherwise valid task, and if authors skip self-check the task silently scores every arm identically.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep cwd on sys.path (e.g. pass `-e PYTHONPATH=/workspace` in the container / `PYTHONPATH=<tree>` on host, or drop -P and use `-s` only), or have the seeders prove with the exact same shaped argv the grader uses so divergence is caught at seeding time.

findings.description: Host mode runs `python3 -P -m pytest …`. The -P interpreter flag exists only in Python >= 3.11. On a host with 3.10 or older (Ubuntu 22.04 default) the interpreter exits 2 with `Unknown option: -P` before pytest starts.
findings.failure_mode: Every host-mode suite run returns rc 2 with no summary line → parse_error:true, passed 0, total = static count; grade.json looks like a legitimate all-fail grade rather than a tool error (exit 2 is only raised by GradeError paths).
findings.suggested_fix: Guard on `sys.version_info` at startup (the same guard the tarfile filter needs) and fail with GradeError, or probe `python3 -P -c pass` once in docker_ready()/a host_ready() and refuse with exit 2.

findings.description: exec_in_tree returns any rc as a test result. `docker run` reports its own failures as 125 (daemon/mount error), 126 (command not invocable) and 127 (command not found, e.g. no `timeout` in the image); SELinux or rootless-docker bind-mount denials surface as an immediate non-zero exit with an error message rather than test output. run_suite then takes the no-summary branch and records passed=0, total=max(static,1), parse_error:true.
findings.failure_mode: Infrastructure failures after docker_ready() passed are written to grade.json as a plausible all-fail grade and joined into runs.jsonl by ablation-row.sh, biasing the ablation rather than aborting with exit 2 as the header promises for 'a tool failure'.
findings.suggested_fix: In container mode treat rc in (125,126,127) with no parseable summary as GradeError; optionally run a one-shot `docker run … <image> timeout 1 true` smoke in docker_ready() to validate the mount/user/tmpfs combination before grading.

findings.description: On the outer `subprocess.run(timeout=TEST_TIMEOUT_S+60)` expiry only the `docker run` client process is killed. The container (and the in-container `timeout 120` child, if it ignored SIGTERM) keeps running with `<run-dir>/grading/<tree>` bind-mounted rw; `--rm` only fires when the container itself exits.
findings.failure_mode: Leaked containers keep writing into the grading tree after the grader has moved on; a re-grade's fresh_dir(grading) can race with or fail against files still being created, and repeated batches accumulate orphan containers.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `--name` (derived from a uuid) and on TimeoutExpired run `docker kill <name>`; alternatively add `--stop-timeout` and use `docker run --init` so the inner timeout reliably terminates the process group.

findings.description: copy_tree hardens against FIFOs, sockets and symlinks but not against unreadable regular files. A sandbox file left at mode 0o000 (a common residue of permission-handling tests) makes `shutil.copyfile(sp, dp)` raise PermissionError, which is not caught anywhere in grade().
findings.failure_mode: The whole grade aborts via the generic `except Exception` → 'internal error' exit 2, so a run is left without grade.json because of content the graded agent controls; the header's 'a FIFO never blocks the copy' robustness claim does not extend to this case.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the copyfile in try/except OSError (skip the file, optionally record it under a `copy_skipped` count), or chmod u+r the source before copying when the grader owns it.

findings.description: With `-rA`, pytest prints captured stdout/stderr sections for passed tests too. OUTCOME_RX (`^(PASSED|FAILED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS) (\S+)`) is applied to every output line, so any captured line beginning with e.g. `FAILED foo` or `ERROR something` (a test exercising a logger or CLI that prints such words) is parsed as a test outcome and added to `bad`.
findings.failure_mode: A spurious bad entry makes all_pass() false and inflates failed_names/total for a tree whose tests all passed; verdict_accuracy flips (an APPROVED gate on a green tree is scored inaccurate) and self-check reference can FAIL.
findings.suggested_fix: Only parse outcome lines after the `short test summary info` header (or stop at the final `=== N passed … ===` line), e.g. locate the summary section by its `=+ short test summary info =+` marker and restrict OUTCOME_RX to that slice.

findings.description: The contamination root set is chosen by the grader's own `--executor`, not by how the graded run executed. With the default container executor, `/home/evaluser` is wholesale allowed; if the pipeline ran the agent on the host (sandbox under /home/evaluser/.cache/…), absolute reads of sibling run-dir paths (`<run-dir>/eval/adversarial-review.json`, `meta/`, other runs' sandboxes) are inside an allowed root and never flagged as outside_path, while the transcripts' init cwd already reveals which model applies.
findings.failure_mode: outside_path detection is silently disabled for host-executed runs graded in container mode, so D-4.7 contamination (an agent reading its own dissent envelopes or a sibling run) is reported as null.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the path model from the transcripts: if every init cwd is `/workspace` use the container roots, otherwise use the host roots built from the observed cwds and <run-dir>/sandbox, independent of A.executor.
